headline: 4 truncated images (3 train, 1 val) will crash the dataloader or silently corrupt your val metrics — delete them before training; 2 train images are also missing label files.
training_impact: Training as-is: the dataloader will either abort the epoch on the truncated files or skip them with a warning that is easy to miss in a long log. The one corrupt image in val (val/000000539883) breaks the validation pass, so the mAP you use for the go/no-go decision is computed on a set that can't be read — the number is not trustworthy. Separately, the 2 unlabelled train images are treated as pure background, which suppresses recall for whatever objects they contain.

decisions.rationale: Exact detector, verified: all 4 files are truncated and fail to decode (OSError: image file is truncated, 15-62 bytes unprocessed), while their label files are intact and valid — pure media corruption. 3 in train, 1 in val. A corrupt image aborts the epoch in most training loops or is skipped with an easy-to-miss warning; the val one means your validation metric is computed on a broken set. Fix: delete all 4 image+label pairs (train/000000076547, train/000000140987, train/000000271116, val/000000539883) or re-export them from the source. This is the only thing that blocks the run.

Exact detector, verified: train/000000303713 and train/000000577976 have no .txt file. Ultralytics treats an image with no label as a pure background image, so if these actually contain objects the model is being explicitly taught to ignore them — a silent recall hit on those classes. Fix: check the two images; if they contain objects, annotate them; if they are genuinely empty scenes, create empty .txt files to make the intent explicit. Only 2 of 468 train images, so the cost is small, but it is a real defect, not a cosmetic one.
